mainTopic: Whether night counts toward the time of a קרבן (the זב on the night of the eighth), and how a woman with many births or discharges brings her offerings.
overview: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: בית הלל learn from the extra word ״לְבַת״ that a woman who miscarries on the night of her 81st day must bring another קרבן. רבי הושעיא asks בר קפרא whether the same applies to a זב who sees three sightings on the night of his eighth day. בר קפרא answers that the rule rests on that special verse, so it covers only the יולדת. The גמרא then asks whether two ברייתות argue about the זב depending on whether night is מחוסר זמן. רבי אלעזר says both agree that night is מחוסר זמן; they simply speak about different kinds of זב. רבי יוחנן's ruling about sightings split between night and day is then examined, and the גמרא shows it follows the view that night is מחוסר זמן. Its new point is that one night sighting still combines with two daytime sightings. A new משנה teaches that a woman with many births or discharges brings one קרבן, and tells how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל brought down the price of birds. The גמרא then brings the dispute between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and רבי עקיבא over how she words her offering. רבא explains it as חטאת against טבילה, and רב פפא begins to challenge that explanation, a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse source for בית הלל's night rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that בית הלל learn from the word ״לְבַת״ that the night of the 81st day counts for a new קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: The verse says 'for a daughter.' This comes to include the night of the eighty-first day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the verse source for בית הלל's opinion in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית הלל say that a woman who miscarries on the night before her 81st day must bring an extra קרבן, and בית שמאי exempt her. Here בית הלל explain that the word ״לְבַת״ in the verse is extra. That extra word teaches that even the night of the 81st day is included.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For a daughter.' A word in the verse about the יולדת's קרבן, which בית הלל treat as extra.
To include. Used when an extra word in a verse adds a case.
The night (evening) that begins the 81st day.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
Behold, it (the verse) says: "for a daughter"
to include the night of the eighty-first day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by giving the verse source for בית הלל's position in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra word ״לְבַת״ includes the night of the 81st day, so a miscarriage then requires a new קרבן.

steps.title: רבי הושעיא asks about a זב on the night of the eighth
steps.stepSummary: After leaving בר קפרא for רבי חייא, רבי הושעיא meets בר קפרא and asks him how בית הלל would rule about a זב who sees three sightings on the night of his eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הושעיא used to learn before בר קפרא. He left him and went to learn before רבי חייא. One day he met בר קפרא and asked him: A זב saw three sightings on the night of the eighth day. What do בית הלל say about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a new question: does בית הלל's night rule also apply to a זב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב who saw three sightings brings a קרבן on his eighth day, after seven clean days. The question is about new sightings on the night before that eighth day. Is that night like the night of the 81st for a יולדת, so that he must bring another קרבן?

keyTerms.meaning: Regularly found; here it means he learned there often.
He left him.
A man with a type of bodily discharge. After three sightings he must bring a קרבן.
Sightings, meaning occurrences of the discharge.
The night that begins the eighth day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hoshaya was regularly found
before bar Kappara (learning from him).
He left him and came
before Rabbi Chiyya.
One day he met him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' means בר קפרא, his old teacher.

phrases.english: he asked of him:
A zav who saw three sightings
on the night of the eighth day,

phrases.aramaic: מָה בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים בְּדָבָר זֶה?
phrases.english: what do Beit Hillel say about this matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד פְּגַע בֵּיהּ, בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes בית הלל's night rule from step 1 and asks whether it extends to a זב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בית הלל would require a זב who saw three sightings on the night of the eighth to bring an additional קרבן.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: רבי הושעיא explains his doubt. Maybe בית הלל's rule comes only from the extra verse, so the זב is exempt. Or maybe there is no difference between the cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is בית הלל's reason for the woman who miscarries at night only because it says 'for a daughter'? Then for a זב who saw three sightings on the night of the eighth, they would exempt him, since there is no extra verse for him. Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי הושעיא spells out both possible ways to understand בית הלל, which is why his question is a real doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the night counts only because the extra word ״לְבַת״ says so, and the זב has no such extra verse, so he is exempt. Side two: ״לְבַת״ only shows a general idea, that the night before the day of the קרבן already counts. That idea would apply to a זב too.

keyTerms.meaning: Their reason.
A woman who miscarries.
They exempt.
Extra verses, from which a law can be learned.
Or perhaps there is no difference. Introduces the second side of a doubt.

phrases.english: Is the reason of Beit Hillel
regarding a woman who miscarries at night
because it is written: "for a daughter"?
But a zav who saw three sightings
on the night of the eighth day, they exempt him,
since there are no extra verses (for him).
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two possible sides of the question asked in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is בית הלל's night rule a special verse-based rule for the יולדת, or a general principle that also covers a זב?

steps.title: בר קפרא asks what רבי חייא says
steps.stepSummary: Instead of answering, בר קפרא asks what 'the Babylonian' says, and רבי הושעיא stays silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to him: What does the Babylonian say about this? רבי הושעיא was silent and said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא turns the question back on רבי הושעיא and asks what his new teacher, רבי חייא, says. רבי הושעיא has nothing to answer, which sets up בר קפרא's own answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a real legal question. It is a pointed jab, because רבי הושעיא left בר קפרא to learn with רבי חייא. His silence shows that his new teacher had not settled the question for him.

keyTerms.meaning: The Babylonian. Here it refers to רבי חייא, who came from בבל.
He was silent.
Anything; here, 'nothing at all.'

phrases.english: Bar Kappara said to him:
What does the Babylonian say about this matter?
phrases.notes: He means רבי חייא, who came from בבל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hoshaya was silent,
he did not say anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי הושעיא's question with a counter-question instead of an answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי חייא holds about the זב on the night of the eighth.

steps.title: בר קפרא answers from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא says we do not need רבי חייא. Going back to the ברייתא, the extra word ״לְבַת״ includes the night of the 81st, so the rule depends on that verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to him: Do we need the words of עייא (חייא)? Let us go back to the earlier teaching: the verse says 'for a daughter' to include the night of the eighty-first day.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא answers the question himself by repeating the ברייתא from step 1. The rule for the night comes from a special extra word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא really repeats the words of the ברייתא here, this time as proof. Since בית הלל needed the extra word ״לְבַת״ to include the night, the rule is a special one for the יולדת. A זב has no such extra verse, so he would be exempt. This is the first side of רבי הושעיא's doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we need?
A form of the name חייא.
Let us go back to the earlier words.

steps.whatToRemember: According to בר קפרא, בית הלל's rule that the night counts for a new קרבן comes only from the extra word ״לְבַת״. So it applies to the יולדת and not to a זב.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a copy of step 1. The same words now serve as the answer: because a verse was needed, the rule cannot be stretched to a זב.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara said to him:
Do we need the words of Iyya?
Let us go back to the earlier words:
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from the start of the גמרא.

phrases.english: Behold, it says: "for a daughter"
to include the night of the eighty-first day.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכִין לְדִבְרֵי עִיָּיא? נַחְזוֹר עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי הושעיא's silence, בר קפרא gives his own answer by going back to the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The night rule comes from a special extra word for the יולדת. With no such verse for a זב, he is exempt.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בית הלל's night rule is limited to the יולדת because it rests on the extra word ״לְבַת״.

steps.title: Maybe two ברייתות argue about this exact question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our question is a dispute between תנאים. One ברייתא says the זב brings another קרבן and one says he does not, depending on whether night counts as מחוסר זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute of תנאים. About a זב who saw three sightings on the night of the eighth day, one ברייתא says he brings, and another ברייתא says he does not bring. Isn't it a dispute? The one who says 'he brings' holds that night is not 'lacking time,' and the one who says 'he does not bring' holds that night is 'lacking time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the question asked in Step 2 is already argued about by two ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זב's קרבן cannot be brought at night. So the question is whether the night of the eighth day already counts as his 'time.' If night is not מחוסר זמן, the new sightings come after his time arrived, and they start a new obligation. If night is מחוסר זמן, he is still inside the old obligation, so there is no new קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is a dispute between תנאים
Lacking time: the time for the קרבן has not yet come
The night before the eighth day
Sightings, meaning discharges of זיבה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Night of the eighth' means the night BEFORE the eighth day, because the Jewish day starts at night.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of tannaim:
a zav who saw three sightings
on the night of the eighth day,
one baraita teaches: he brings another offering,
and the other one teaches: he does not bring.
Is it not a dispute of tannaim?
For the one that teaches 'he brings'
holds: night is not 'lacking time,'
phrases.notes: He means the night already counts as the time for his קרבן, even though it can't be offered until morning.

phrases.english: and the one that teaches 'he does not bring'
holds: night is 'lacking time'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question from Step 2 and tries to tie it to a dispute between ברייתות
steps.raayaObject: Whether the night of the eighth day counts as מחוסר זמן
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות that disagree about a זב who sees three sightings on the night of the eighth

steps.title: Both ברייתות agree; they speak about different kinds of זב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says both תנאים hold that night is מחוסר זמן. The ברייתא that says 'he brings' is talking about a זב of two sightings, and the one that says 'he does not bring' is talking about a זב of three sightings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר אחא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: these תנאים both hold that night is 'lacking time.' The ברייתא that says 'he brings' is about a זב who had two sightings. The ברייתא that says 'he does not bring' is about a זב who had three sightings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the idea of a dispute. Both ברייתות agree, and each one is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב of two sightings does not bring a קרבן at all, so after his count he is fully finished. New sightings are a fresh start that brings a קרבן. A זב of three sightings already owes a קרבן, and its time has not come at night. So the new sightings do not add another one.

keyTerms.meaning: A זב who had two sightings (impure, but no קרבן)
A זב who had three sightings (owes a קרבן)

steps.whyThisMatters: According to רבי אלעזר, there is no argument between תנאים here. Both ברייתות agree that night is מחוסר זמן, and the different rulings come from two different kinds of זב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Acha said that Rabbi Elazar said:
These tannaim both hold
that night is 'lacking time.'
And the one that teaches 'he brings'
is about a zav who had two sightings,
and the one that teaches 'he does not bring'
is about a zav who had three sightings.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי סָבְרִי לַיְלָה מְחוּסַּר זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of a dispute by dividing the cases
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתות argue about whether night is מחוסר זמן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתות can be speaking about different kinds of זב, so they don't have to argue

steps.title: Why teach the obvious two-sighting case?
steps.stepSummary: If the 'he brings' ברייתא is about a זב of two sightings, it seems obvious. Why say it at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: A זב of two sightings: what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new explanation. That ברייתא would be teaching something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A two-sighting זב owes nothing, so new sightings are clearly a fresh case of זיבה. A ברייתא should not need to tell us that.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it? (It seems obvious)

phrases.aramaic: זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא?
phrases.english: A zav who had two sightings: what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the 'he brings' ברייתא speaks about a two-sighting זב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is obvious, so a ברייתא would not need to teach it

steps.title: It teaches: only on the night of the eighth, not on the seventh day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that he brings a קרבן only if he saw on the night of the eighth. A sighting on the seventh day only breaks his count of clean days and does not lead to a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: specifically if he saw on the night of the eighth. But if he saw in the daytime of the seventh day, no. The תנא holds that any sighting that breaks the count does not lead to a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא does teach something new: the timing matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sightings come on the seventh day, he is still counting his seven clean days. Those sightings just ruin the count, and the תנא holds they never create a קרבן obligation. Only after the count is fully done, on the night of the eighth, is this a fresh case that brings a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Specifically, only
A sighting that breaks (cancels) the count of clean days

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
only if he saw on the night of the eighth,
but in the daytime of the seventh, no.
He holds: any sighting that breaks the count
does not lead to an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling contains a hidden new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about a two-sighting זב teaches nothing new
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that only sightings after the count is finished bring a קרבן. Sightings that break the count do not.

steps.title: Why isn't this case in the list of 'five who bring one קרבן'?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if a three-sighting זב who sees again at night brings only one קרבן, the משנה listing five people who bring one קרבן for many sins should have included him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: why did you explain the 'he does not bring' ברייתא as being about a זב of three sightings? If so, let the תנא list it with 'five people bring one קרבן for many sins'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רבי אלעזר's reading from a different angle. If it were right, this case should show up in a known list in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי אלעזר, a three-sighting זב who sees more on the night of the eighth brings just one קרבן for all the sightings. That is exactly the type of case listed in the משנה of 'five who bring one קרבן for many sins.' So why is he missing from it?

keyTerms.meaning: You explained it as speaking about (a certain case)
Let him teach it together with
Five who bring one קרבן (a list in a משנה)

phrases.english: Rava said: Why did you explain
the one that teaches 'he does not bring'
as being about a zav of three sightings?
Let him teach it together with
'Five bring one offering
for many transgressions'!
phrases.notes: This is a list in a משנה in the next פרק (on 9a).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי אלעזר's reading in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the 'he does not bring' ברייתא as a three-sighting זב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the case belongs in the משנה's list of 'one קרבן for many sins,' but it is not there

steps.title: The rule is not clear-cut, so it was left out of the list
steps.stepSummary: The case is not a simple, across-the-board rule. As רבי יוחנן says, the result depends on how the sightings split between night and day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not clear-cut. As רבי יוחנן said: if he saw one at night and two in the day, he brings. If he saw two at night and one in the day, he does not bring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא: the list only includes simple, fixed rules, and this case is not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A three-sighting זב who sees on the eighth does not always bring just one קרבן. It depends on the split. With one sighting at night and two by day, he brings a new קרבן. With two at night and one by day, he does not. Since there is no single answer, the משנה could not list it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not clear-cut; not a fixed rule in every case

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות agree that night is מחוסר זמן. 'He brings' is about a two-sighting זב after his count is finished. 'He does not bring' is about a three-sighting זב. That case is left out of the 'five' list because, as רבי יוחנן shows, it depends on the night/day split.

phrases.english: It is not clear-cut,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה אַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה וּשְׁתַּיִם בַּיּוֹם – מֵבִיא,
phrases.english: If he saw one at night and two in the day, he brings;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתַּיִם בַּלַּיְלָה וְאַחַת בַּיּוֹם – אֵין מֵבִיא.
phrases.english: two at night and one in the day, he does not bring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: The rule is not fixed, so it does not fit a list of fixed rules
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three-sighting case should be in the 'five' list
steps.terutzMaskana: It depends on how the sightings split between night and day, so it could not be listed

steps.title: Proof that one night sighting and two day sightings combine
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues that one sighting at night plus two by day requires a קרבן, just as a זב's weak first sighting combines with two later ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: You can see that one sighting at night and two in the day obligates him to bring a קרבן. A זב's first sighting alone counts only like שכבת זרע, yet when he sees two more, they join together with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a logical proof for רבי יוחנן's ruling that one sighting at night and two by day require another קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single זיבה sighting alone does not make someone a זב. It is treated like שכבת זרע, yet it still joins with two later sightings to create full זב status. רב יוסף reasons the same way here: the night sighting is weak alone, but it can still join the two daytime sightings.

keyTerms.meaning: Know / you can see. Introduces a logical proof.
The first sighting of a discharge
A seminal emission. It brings only a one-day טומאה.
They combine / join together

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Know that if he saw one at night
and two in the day, he brings a קרבן,
phrases.notes: "Night" and "day" here mean the night before the eighth day and the eighth day itself.

phrases.english: for the first sighting
is merely like semen,
and yet if he sees two other ones,
they combine with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּדַע דְּאַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה וּשְׁתַּיִם בַּיּוֹם מֵבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports one detail of רבי יוחנן's night/day breakdown cited in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that one sighting at night plus two by day requires a קרבן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The general rule that a זב's first sighting, though only like שכבת זרע, still combines with two later sightings

steps.title: The comparison does not hold
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי rejects the proof. A first sighting happens at a time when a קרבן can be owed, but a night sighting does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי said: Are these cases really alike? A זב's first sighting happens at a time when he can become obligated in a קרבן. The night sighting does not happen at such a time. If רבי יוחנן had not taught us that it combines, I would have said it does not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי knocks down רב יוסף's proof. He does not reject רבי יוחנן's ruling itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב's first sighting can still lead to a קרבן, so it makes sense that it combines. A sighting on the night before the eighth day cannot lead to a קרבן on its own. So logic alone would say it does not combine. We know it does only because רבי יוחנן told us so.

keyTerms.meaning: Are the cases comparable? Used to reject a comparison.
A time when one can become obligated (here, in a קרבן)
I would have thought (an initial assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not arguing with רבי יוחנן's ruling. He agrees the sightings combine. He is only saying that רב יוסף's 'proof' is not a real proof. The ruling stands only because רבי יוחנן said it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said:
Are the cases comparable?
The first sighting of a זב:
he saw it at a time of liability.
But one sighting at night:
since he did not see it at a time of liability,
phrases.notes: He means that sightings on the night before the eighth day cannot obligate a new קרבן.

phrases.english: were it not that רבי יוחנן taught us
that it combines,
I would have said it does not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's proof from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רבי יוחנן's ruling remains.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two sightings are not alike. The first sighting comes at a time when a קרבן can be owed, but the night sighting does not.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן really hold night is lacking time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי יוחנן treats night as מחוסר זמן. In the case of a נזיר, he rules that becoming טמא at night still requires a new קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוחנן really say that night is מחוסר זמן? But חזקיה said: if he became טמא in the day, he brings a קרבן; if at night, he does not. And רבי יוחנן said: even at night, he brings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the assumption behind רבי יוחנן's night/day breakdown. Elsewhere, רבי יוחנן says night is NOT considered too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's ruling for the זב treats night sightings as weaker. That suggests night is מחוסר זמן, too early for a קרבן. But in a dispute with חזקיה, רבי יוחנן rules that becoming טמא at night does lead to a new קרבן. That implies night counts as a proper time. This looks like a contradiction in רבי יוחנן's views.

keyTerms.meaning: Lacking time: the proper time for the קרבן has not yet arrived
And did he really say? Opens a challenge from the same sage's other statement.
He became ritually impure

steps.whyThisMatters: This contradiction forces the גמרא to ask whether רבי יוחנן's ruling about the זב reflects his own view. The next step answers that it does not.

phrases.english: And did רבי יוחנן really say
that night is lacking time?
But didn't חזקיה say:
if he became impure in the day, he brings,
phrases.notes: This is about a נזיר who became טמא again on his eighth day, when his קרבן was due.

phrases.english: if at night, he does not bring.
And רבי יוחנן said:
Even at night, he brings!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לַיְלָה מְחוּסַּר זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from discussing רב יוסף's proof to challenging the basic assumption behind רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יוחנן holds night is מחוסר זמן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In his dispute with חזקיה about a נזיר, רבי יוחנן says becoming טמא at night obligates a new קרבן. This shows he does not treat night as מחוסר זמן, which contradicts his ruling for the זב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was speaking for another opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's ruling that 'two at night and one by day' brings no קרבן follows the view that night is מחוסר זמן. It is not necessarily his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן said 'two at night and one by day, he does not bring,' he said it according to the one who holds that night is still 'missing time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 14. רבי יוחנן's ruling about the night sightings was said according to someone else's opinion, not his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of the נזיר, רבי יוחנן himself holds that night is NOT מחוסר זמן. So his ruling about the זב only works for those who do treat night as מחוסר זמן. That removes the contradiction between his two rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Missing time': the time for bringing the קרבן has not arrived yet
'According to the one who says': a ruling given for someone else's opinion

phrases.english: When Rabbi Yochanan says:
"Two at night and one by day, he does not bring"
phrases.notes: The night and day here belong to the eighth day, when the זב would normally bring his קרבן.

phrases.english: that is according to the one who says [night is] 'missing time.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 14 between רבי יוחנן's ruling on the זב and his ruling on the נזיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the ruling follows another opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן personally holds that night is מחוסר זמן
steps.terutzMaskana: He spoke for the view that night is מחוסר זמן. In his own view, night is not.

steps.title: If so, the ruling seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the ruling only follows the view that night is מחוסר זמן, then of course night sightings bring no קרבן. Why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says that? That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If רבי יוחנן was only applying that view, he seems to be telling us nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the view that night is מחוסר זמן, a sighting at night cannot create a new קרבן. So 'two at night and one by day brings nothing' follows automatically. The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן's statement adds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It's obvious!': a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new

phrases.english: According to the one who says [this]? It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן was only applying the view that night is מחוסר זמן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he was only applying that view, his ruling follows automatically and teaches nothing.

steps.title: The real point is that a night sighting still combines
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן needed to teach the other case: one sighting at night plus two by day. The night sighting still joins the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed it for the case where he saw once at night and twice by day. You might have said: since he saw it when no קרבן could be owed, it should not join with the others. So he teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what is new in רבי יוחנן's teaching. One sighting at night does join two daytime sightings to require a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought a sighting at a time when no קרבן can be owed is simply ignored. רבי יוחנן teaches that it still counts toward the three sightings. It just cannot create a קרבן on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needed it': this is the case that holds the real new teaching
'You might have said': introduces a mistaken assumption
A time when one can become obligated to bring a קרבן
To combine or join together with others
'It teaches us': the new lesson

steps.whatToRemember: According to the view that night is מחוסר זמן: two sightings at night plus one by day bring no new קרבן. But one at night plus two by day DO combine and require one.

phrases.english: [Where] he saw one at night and two by day:
that is what he needed [to teach].
You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו בִּזְמַן חִיּוּבָא קָחָזֵי לֵיהּ –
phrases.english: since he did not see it at a time of obligation,
it should not combine [with the others];
so he teaches us [that it does].

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה אַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה וּשְׁתַּיִם בַּיּוֹם אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by pointing to the other case in רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The new teaching lies in a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sighting at a time when no קרבן can be owed does not count at all
steps.terutzMaskana: A night sighting does combine with two daytime sightings to require a קרבן

steps.title: משנה: a woman with five births or discharges
steps.stepSummary: With five doubtful births or discharges, a woman brings one קרבן, may eat קדשים, and owes nothing more. With five definite ones, she brings one קרבן to eat קדשים but still owes the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who has five doubtful births, or five doubtful discharges, brings one קרבן. Then she may eat from קדשים, and she does not owe the rest. If she has five definite discharges or five definite births, she brings one קרבן and may eat קדשים, but she still owes the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the rule for a woman who owes many bird offerings after births or discharges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One קרבן is enough to let her eat קדשים again in both cases. The difference is what remains. Doubtful cases need nothing more, but definite cases leave her still owing the other offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
Doubt: we are not sure the event really obligates her
Birth, which requires the mother to bring a קרבן
A discharge of blood that makes a woman a זבה
Definite, certain
She may eat from קדשים (meat of offerings)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman who has upon her

phrases.aramaic: סְפֵק חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וּסְפֵק חָמֵשׁ זִיבוֹת –
phrases.english: five doubtful births, or five doubtful discharges,
brings one offering
and may eat from offerings,
and the rest are not an obligation on her.

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵשׁ זִיבוֹת וַדָּאוֹת וְחָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדָּאוֹת –
phrases.english: [If she has] five definite discharges or five definite births,
she brings one offering
and may eat from offerings,
and the rest are an obligation on her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ סְפֵק חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the זב is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One קרבן lets her eat קדשים. For doubtful cases nothing more is owed. For definite cases the rest are still owed.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל brings down the price of birds
steps.stepSummary: When bird pairs cost a gold דינר, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught that even five definite cases need only one קרבן, and the price fell to a quarter of a silver דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, pairs of birds in ירושלים cost a gold דינר. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: 'By this Dwelling, I will not go to sleep tonight until they cost silver דינרים!' He went into the בית דין and taught: 'A woman with five definite births or five definite discharges brings one קרבן, may eat קדשים, and does not owe the rest.' That same day the price of bird pairs dropped to a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story. A leading sage gave a lenient ruling so that women could afford their offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demand for bird offerings pushed prices very high. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught that even in definite cases the extra offerings are not owed. That is more lenient than the line just before it, and with fewer birds needed, the price crashed that same day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Nests': pairs of birds brought as offerings
A gold דינר, worth many silver דינרים
'By this Dwelling': an oath by the בית המקדש, the place of the שכינה
A quarter (of a silver דינר)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rulings. The line just before this says that with definite cases 'the rest ARE an obligation.' רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught that 'the rest are NOT an obligation,' and the story shows he did this to bring down the price of birds.
steps.whatToRemember: One קרבן always lets her eat קדשים again. Whether she still owes the rest depends on doubtful versus definite cases, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught a lenient ruling to keep offerings affordable.

phrases.english: There was an incident where nests stood in Jerusalem
at a gold dinar.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
[I swear by] this Dwelling,
I will not go to sleep tonight
until it is at [silver] dinars!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, בסוף ('in the end'), and some have the word in square brackets, כסף ('silver').

phrases.english: He entered the court and taught:
"A woman who has upon her

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדָּאוֹת חָמֵשׁ זִיבוֹת וַדָּאוֹת –
phrases.english: five definite births or five definite discharges
brings one offering
and may eat from offerings,
and the rest are not an obligation on her."
And nests stood that day at a quarter.
phrases.notes: He means a quarter of a silver dinar, a huge drop from a gold dinar.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָמְדוּ קִינִּין בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם בְּדִינַר זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story connected to the משנה's rule about definite births and discharges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with five definite births or discharges, she brings one קרבן, may eat קדשים, and does not owe the rest.

steps.title: Two bird-pairs for mixed definite and doubtful cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. A woman with five definite births plus five doubtful births or discharges brings two קינין, one for the definite cases and one for the doubtful cases. The definite one is eaten and she still owes the rest. The doubtful one is not eaten and she owes nothing more for the doubtful cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If a woman has five definite births and five doubtful discharges, or five definite births and five doubtful births, she brings two pairs of birds. One pair is for the definite cases and one is for the doubtful cases. The pair brought for the definite cases is eaten, and she still owes the remaining offerings. The pair brought for the doubtful cases is not eaten, and she does not owe the remaining offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a woman who has both definite and doubtful obligations at the same time. It explains how she handles each group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on step 18, which treated all-definite and all-doubtful cases separately. Here the two kinds are mixed, so she needs one קן for each kind. The קן for the definite cases is a real offering, so the כהנים eat it, and she still owes the other definite offerings. The קן for the doubtful cases may not be needed at all, so it is not eaten, and nothing more is owed for the doubtful cases.

keyTerms.meaning: births
discharges that make a woman a זבה
definite, certain
doubtful, uncertain
pairs of bird offerings (plural of קֵן)
an obligation she still owes

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדַּאי חָמֵשׁ זִיבוֹת סָפֵק
phrases.english: Five definite births and five doubtful discharges

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדַּאי וְחָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת סָפֵק –
phrases.english: or five definite births and five doubtful births –
she brings two pairs of birds,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת עַל הַוַּדַּאי וְאַחַת עַל הַסָּפֵק,
phrases.english: one for the definite and one for the doubtful,
the one for the definite is eaten
and the rest remain an obligation on her,
the one for the doubtful is not eaten
and the rest are not an obligation on her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדַּאי חָמֵשׁ זִיבוֹת סָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rules from step 18 to a woman who has both definite and doubtful cases at once.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed definite and doubtful cases need two קינין. The definite one is eaten and the rest are still owed. The doubtful one is not eaten and nothing more is owed.

steps.title: How she should word her offerings: name the last birth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says that for the definite cases she should say the offering is 'for the last one'. For the doubtful cases, she names the definite one if there is one among them; if not, she may name any one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: For the definite cases, she should say, 'This is for the last one,' and she is cleared. For the doubtful cases, if there is a definite one among them, she should say, 'This is for the definite one,' and she is cleared. If there is not, she should say, 'This is for one of them,' and she is cleared.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי adds a rule about the words the woman must say when she designates her offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For definite obligations, the wording is strict: she must name the last birth. For doubtful obligations, she names the definite case if one is mixed in. Otherwise any one of them will do. Step 24 will explain why the last one matters.

keyTerms.meaning: the last one
and she is cleared / released
among them

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
For the definite, she should say:
'For the last one,' and she is cleared.
phrases.notes: He means the last birth in time. Step 24 explains why that one matters.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל סָפֵק, אִם יֵשׁ וַדַּאי בֵּינֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: For the doubtful, if there is a definite one among them,
she should say: 'For the definite one,' and she is cleared,
and if not, she should say:
'For one of them,' and she is cleared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new opinion about how she words her offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For definite obligations she must name the last one. For doubtful obligations she names the definite case if there is one, and otherwise any one of them.

steps.title: Any one of them is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. For both definite and doubtful cases, she may simply say the offering is 'for one of them'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Whether for the definite or for the doubtful, she should say, 'This is for one of them,' and she is cleared.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the opposing view: there is no need to name the last birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא uses the same simple wording for every case. He sees no special importance in which birth she names. This sets up the dispute that רבא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: whether... or
one of them (any one)

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין עַל הַוַּדַּאי בֵּין עַל הַסָּפֵק,
phrases.english: whether for the definite or for the doubtful,
she should say: 'For one of them,' and she is cleared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In every case she may name any one of the births.

steps.title: What is the root of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק tells רב פפא that he will quote רבא, who asks what these two תנאים are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רב פפא: Let me tell you something in the name of רבא. What are these תנאים arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the underlying reason behind the argument between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two views differ only in wording, but רבא wants to show a deeper principle that drives each one. The answer comes in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, sages of the משנה period
about what do they argue?
in the name of

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rav Pappa,
let me tell you in the name of Rava:
these Tannaim, about what do they argue?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the dispute in steps 21 and 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle leads each תנא to his view about how she words her offering?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי compares it to a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats these offerings like a חטאת. A person who owes five חטאות must bring all of them, and the last one completes his atonement. So she must name the last birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי compares them to a חטאת. Someone who owes five חטאות must bring all of them, and at the end he is atoned. Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains רבי יוחנן בן נורי's reasoning by comparing the woman's offerings to sin offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a חטאת, atonement is complete only after the final offering. In the same way, only the offering for her last birth completes her process. That is why רבי יוחנן בן נורי requires her to name the last one.

keyTerms.meaning: compares
sin offering
atones
it is no different

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי מְדַמֵּי לְהוֹן לְחַטָּאת,
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri compares them to a sin offering,
for one who owes five sin offerings
until he brings all of them
and the end atones for him,
here too it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי מְדַמֵּי לְהוֹן לְחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 for רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He compares her offerings to חטאות, where the final offering completes atonement. So she must name the last birth.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא compares it to immersions
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא treats these offerings like טבילות. A person who needs five immersions becomes pure after immersing once. So any one offering is enough, and she may name any one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא compares them to immersions. Someone who needs five immersions becomes pure once he immerses one time. Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains רבי עקיבא's reasoning by comparing the woman's offerings to immersions in a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טבילה, one immersion takes care of every cause of impurity at once, so there is no 'last one'. In the same way, one offering lets her eat קדשים, no matter which birth she names. This completes רבא's explanation: חטאת versus טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: immersions in a מקוה
one time
he became pure

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute comes down to one comparison. רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats her offerings like a חטאת, where the last offering finishes the atonement, so she names the last birth. רבי עקיבא treats them like טבילה, where one immersion purifies, so she may name any birth.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva compares them to immersions,
for one who is obligated in five immersions,
once he immerses one time he is pure,
here too it is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's answer by giving רבי עקיבא's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He compares her offerings to טבילות, where one immersion purifies. So any one offering works and she may name any birth.

steps.title: רב פפא questions the חטאת comparison
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks: if רבי יוחנן בן נורי compares these offerings to a חטאת, why can she simply say 'for one of them' in the doubtful cases? He begins comparing her to a person obligated in חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to him: If you think that רבי יוחנן בן נורי compares these offerings to a חטאת, why should she be able to say 'for one of them' for the doubtful births and be exempt? After all, a person who is obligated...
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבא's explanation of רבי יוחנן בן נורי. He also starts building a comparison to a person who owes חטאות, and that comparison continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that for רבי יוחנן בן נורי, every offering must be brought and the last one is what finishes the atonement, just like a חטאת. But in the doubtful cases, רבי יוחנן בן נורי let her name any one of them, which sounds like one offering is enough. רב פפא says this does not fit the חטאת model.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you really think that). This sets up an idea in order to challenge it.
Compares, treats one thing as similar to another.
A doubtful case. Here it means a birth or miscarriage that may or may not create an obligation to bring an offering.
She will be exempt, free of her obligation.
Why? Often used to raise a difficulty.

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not arguing with רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling itself. He is challenging רבא's explanation of the reason behind that ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to him:
phrases.notes: He is answering רב נחמן בר יצחק, who just quoted רבא's explanation.

why, for the doubtful ones, should she say:
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule that in doubtful cases she may name any one of them.

phrases.english: "For one of them," and be exempt?
Whereas one who is obligated...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in Step 24 for רבי יוחנן בן נורי's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats birth offerings like a חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the חטאת model, each offering is needed and the last one completes the atonement. But רבי יוחנן בן נורי lets her name any one of the doubtful births and be exempt, which looks more like the טבילות model.
